Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning algorithms implementations. 490 stars   94 forks   Branches   Tags   Activity. MORL-Baselines is a library of Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) algorithms. This repository aims to contain reliable MORL algorithms implementations in PyTorch. An overview of some techniques used in various MORL algorithms is also provided in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Based on Decomposition: A Taxonomy and Framework. A tutorial on MO-Gymnasium and MORL-Baselines is also available: Open in Colab. * Single and multi-policy algorithms under both SER and ESR criteria are implemented. | **Name** | Single/Multi-policy | ESR/SER | Observation space | Action space | Paper |. | GPI-LS + GPI-PD | Multi | SER | Continuous | Discrete / Continuous | Paper and Supplementary Materials |. | MORL/D | Multi | SER / ESR | Discrete / Continuous | Discrete / Continuous | Paper |. | Envelope Q-Learning | Multi | SER | Continuous | Discrete | Paper |. | Pareto Conditioned Networks (PCN) | Multi | SER/ESR 1 | Continuous | Discrete / Continuous | Paper |. | Pareto Q-Learning | Multi | SER | Discrete | Discrete | Paper |. | MO Q learning | Single | SER | Discrete | Discrete | Paper |. | Iterated Pareto Referent Optimisation (IPRO) | Multi | SER | Continuous | Discrete | Paper |. | Iterated Pareto Referent Optimisation-2D (IPRO-2D) 2 | Multi | SER | Continuous | Discrete | Paper |. | Non-Linear Multi-Objective PPO (NLMOPPO) | Single | SER | Continuous | Discrete | Derivation of the policy-gradient update in this paper |. MORL-Baselines participates to Open RL Benchmark which contains tracked experiments from popular RL libraries such as cleanRL and Stable Baselines 3. As much as possible, this repo tries to follow the single-file implementation rule for all algorithms. * `examples/` contains a set of examples to use MORL Baselines with MO-Gymnasium environments. * `multi_policy/` contains the implementations of multi-policy algorithms. * `single_policy/` contains the implementations of single-policy algorithms (ESR and SER). If you use MORL-Baselines in your research, please cite our NeurIPS 2023 paper:. Title: MOPPO (Multi-Objective PPO) | LucasAlegre/morl-baselines | DeepWiki
# MOPPO (Multi-Objective PPO). This document describes MOPPO (Multi-Objective Proximal Policy Optimization), a single-policy multi-objective reinforcement learning algorithm implemented in the MORL-Baselines library. MOPPO extends the standard PPO algorithm to handle multi-objective reward functions through weighted scalarization. This page covers the implementation details, key components, and usage of MOPPO. For more general information about single-policy algorithms, see Single-Policy Algorithms. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py238-242. MOPPO is an adaptation of the popular Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm for multi-objective reinforcement learning. It follows the Scalarized Expected Return (SER) approach, where the multiple objectives are combined using a weighted sum scalarization before optimization. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py238-242. ### MOPPO within MORL-Baselines. Sources: morl\_baselines/common/morl\_algorithm.py23-32 morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py160-235 morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py238-242. ### Actor-Critic Network Architecture. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py160-235. `MOPPONet` is the neural network architecture used by MOPPO, combining:. The network includes specialized initialization functions for different components to stabilize training. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py160-235. The `PPOReplayBuffer` stores transitions collected during training:. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py22-104. ## Training Process. The MOPPO training process follows this sequence:. Key steps in the training process:. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py580-613 morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py390-431 morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py433-476 morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py493-578. MOPPO has numerous hyperparameters for tuning performance:. | `steps_per_iteration` | Steps per training iteration | 2048 |. | `clip_coef` | PPO clipping coefficient | 0.2 |. | `vf_coef` | Value function coefficient | 0.5 |. | `clip_vloss` | Clip value loss | True |. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py244-296. To use MOPPO, you need to:. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py580-613. MOPPO inherits evaluation methods from the `MOPolicy` base class:. Sources: morl\_baselines/common/morl\_algorithm.py82-152. ### Advantage Computation. MOPPO computes vector-valued advantages for each objective, which are then scalarized using the weight vector. It supports both standard returns-based advantages and Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE). When using GAE, the advantages are computed as:. `advantages[t] = delta + gamma * lambda * nextnonterminal * advantages[t+1]`. where `delta = reward_t + gamma * nextvalues * nextnonterminal - value_t`. After computing vector advantages, they are scalarized using weighted sum:. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py433-476. The policy update follows the standard PPO objective with clipping:. Compute the policy loss with clipping:. pg_loss2 = -advantages * clamp(ratio, 1-clip_coef, 1+clip_coef). `v_loss = 0.5 * ||value - returns||^2`. With optional clipping for the value function. `loss = pg_loss - ent_coef * entropy + v_loss * vf_coef`. Sources: morl\_baselines/single\_policy/ser/mo\_ppo.py493-578. results.content: Linear Support is a core component used by many multi-policy algorithms to compute optimal weight vectors when using linear utility functions in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL). They reduce the infinite space of possible weight vectors to a finite set of important ones Sources: morl_baselines/multi_policy/linear_support/linear_support.py 309-363 The `LinearSupport` class is implemented in morl_baselines/multi_policy/linear_support/linear_support.py with the following key properties: ### Key Methods #### Initialization and Weight Selection The class is initialized with the number of objectives and starts with extrema weights (weights where one objective gets all the importance): Sources: morl_baselines/multi_policy/linear_support/linear_support.py 34-57morl_baselines/multi_policy/linear_support/linear_support.py 59-113 #### Adding Solutions When a policy is trained with a specific weight vector, its performance value vector is added to the CCS if it's non-dominated: def add_solution(self, value: np.ndarray, w: np.ndarray) -> List[int]: # Check if dominated by existing solutions # Remove values that become obsolete with this new solution # Add to CCS Sources: morl_baselines/multi_policy/linear_support/linear_support.py 149-175 #### Calculating Priorities The priority of a weight vector determines which corner weight to explore next: 1. **GPI-LS Priority**: Difference between GPI policy value and best known value max_value_gpi = np.dot(max_value_gpi, w) Sources: morl_baselines/multi_policy/linear_support/linear_support.py 177-214 #### Computing Corner Weights Corner weights are computed using computational geometry, specifically the dual of the convex hull problem: def compute_corner_weights(self) -> List[np.ndarray]: # Setup matrices for the polytope A = np.vstack(self.ccs) # ... Sources: morl_baselines/multi_policy/linear_support/linear_support.py 309-363 Linear Support is used by several multi-policy algorithms in MORL-Baselines: Sources: morl_baselines/multi_policy/linear_support/linear_support.py 22-33tests/test_algos.py 18-19tests/test_algos.py 120-149 ### Example Usage The example below demonstrates a basic usage pattern for the Linear Support algorithm, where it guides the exploration of weight vectors for training policies: ols = LinearSupport(num_objectives=2, epsilon=0.1, verbose=False) # Get next weight to explore # Train policy with weight w # ... # Evaluate policy and add to CCS _, _, vec, discounted_vec = new_policy.policy_eval(eval_env=env, weights=w) # Update CCS and remove obsolete policies removed_inds = ols.add_solution(discounted_vec, w) Sources: tests/test_algos.py 120-149 * Optimistic Linear Support (OLS): Section 3.3 of Roijers' thesis () * Generalized Policy Improvement Linear Support (GPI-LS): "GPI-PD with Linear Support for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning" () ### On this page Ask Devin about LucasAlegre/morl-baselines

results.title: Maximum Entropy-Regularized Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning - Rui Zhao 赵瑞
results.content: Research Scientist, Machine Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Game AI, Robotics. # Maximum Entropy-Regularized Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning. In Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning, an agent learns to achieve multiple goals with a goal-conditioned policy. During learning, the agent first collects the trajectories into a replay buffer, and later these trajectories are selected randomly for replay. However, the achieved goals in the replay buffer are often biased towards the behavior policies. From a Bayesian perspective, when there is no prior knowledge about the target goal distribution, the agent should learn uniformly from diverse achieved goals. Therefore, we first propose a novel multi-goal RL objective based on weighted entropy. This objective encourages the agent to maximize the expected return, as well as to achieve more diverse goals. Secondly, we developed a maximum entropy-based prioritization framework to optimize the proposed objective. On a set of multi-goal robotic tasks of OpenAI Gym, we compare our method with other baselines and show promising improvements in both performance and sample-efficiency.
